Before and after each period, 5 min of eyes-open resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) were obtained from a subset of 18 participants (8 female). Functional connectivity was calculated across 16 electrode-pairs in the delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma bands. Beta-band connectivity between the right frontal and right inferior-parietal electrodes increased following CBD (P = 0.001, false discovery rate [FDR]-corrected P [pFDR] = 0.022), and alpha connectivity showed an increase that did not remain following FDR correction (P = 0.036, pFDR = 0.428). No significant differences were observed following placebo for any frequency band (pFDR > 0.69). This study provides preliminary evidence that 12 weeks of cannabidiol is associated with an increase in right fronto-parietal (F4-P8) functional connectivity in autistic children, most pronounced in the beta-band. Replication in larger samples is needed to confirm generalizability and clinical relevance.

title: The Effect of Adding Dexmedetomidine to Modified Del Nido Cardioplegia Solution on Myocardial Protection in Children Undergoing Congenital Heart Defect Surgery - A Prospective, Randomized, Triple-Blind, Controlled Trial.
abstract: The myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is an indispensable factor in pediatric congenital heart defect (CHD) surgery. Although effective myocardial protection strategies are crucial, the issue remains a dilemma. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of adding dexmedetomidine to modified Del Nido cardioplegia on myocardial protection in children undergoing CHD surgery. This was a prospective, randomized, triple-blind, controlled clinical trial. A total of 60 pediatric patients were enrolled and randomized 1:1 into two groups - an intervention group that received dexmedetomidine-enriched modified Del Nido cardioplegia and a control group that received standard modified Del Nido cardioplegia with normal saline. Primary outcomes included serum troponin I and creatine kinase-MB levels, as well as coronary sinus lactate levels. Secondary outcomes were the vasoactive-inotropic score, weaning time from mechanical ventilation, and intensive care unit length of stay. Adding dexmedetomidine to modified Del Nido cardioplegia significantly improved myocardial protection in children undergoing CHD surgery. The intervention group showed significantly lower troponin I levels at all postoperative time points compared to the control group (P < 0.001). Similarly, the dexmedetomidine group had significantly lower vasoactive-inotropic score at all time points (P < 0.001). Patients in the intervention group also experienced a significantly shorter mean ventilator weaning time (P < 0.001) and intensive care unit stay duration (P < 0.001). The overall distribution of postoperative morbidities did not differ significantly between the groups (P = 0.059). Adding dexmedetomidine to modified Del Nido cardioplegia significantly improved myocardial protection in children undergoing corrective CHD surgery.

title: Brain glucose metabolism and blood brain barrier permeability in Alzheimer's disease continuum.
abstract: Within the ATN framework of Alzheimer's disease (AD), patients are classified according to the presence of amyloid pathology (A), tau pathology (T), and neurodegeneration (N). While the A⁺T⁺N⁺ profile is well characterized, the A⁺T⁻N⁺ subgroup remains less understood. This phenotype may reflect mechanisms distinct from tau-driven pathology, potentially involving other amyloid co-pathology such as blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction. We examined A⁺T⁻N⁺ and A⁺T⁺N⁺ patients within the AD continuum (ADc) and cognitively healthy controls. All participants underwent cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarker assessment and 18F-FDG positron emission tomography (FDG-PET). The CSF/serum albumin quotient (QAlb) was used as an index of BBB integrity. Voxel-wise multiple regression analyses evaluated associations between regional glucose metabolism and CSF biomarkers, QAlb, demographics, cognitive status, ApoE genotype, and vascular risk factors (Hypertension, Diabetes, and Hypercholesterolemia). Both AD subgroups showed hypometabolism in temporoparietal Default Mode Network regions. In ADc and A⁺T⁺N⁺ patients, posterior metabolism correlated positively with p-tau and negatively with t-tau. In A⁺T⁻N⁺ individuals, posterior hypometabolism was negatively associated with QAlb and positively with Aβ₄₂. Only Hypertension correlated with metabolism, involving the anterior cingulate cortex in ADc and A⁺T⁺N⁺, but not A⁺T⁻N⁺. Within the AD continuum, A⁺T⁻N⁺ represent a subgroup of patients in whom FDG-PET metabolic dysfunctions appear to be associated with the coexistence of BBB dysfunction alongside amyloid pathology rather than tau-driven mechanisms.

title: Cognitive profile, autistic traits, visual perception, and visual evoked potential findings in Silver-Russell syndrome.
abstract: Silver-Russell syndrome (SRS) is a rare imprinting disorder primarily characterized by growth restriction, but its broader neurodevelopmental phenotype remains incompletely described. We evaluated autistic traits, cognitive function, visuospatial abilities, visual acuity, and visual evoked potentials (VEPs) in children and young adults with SRS. A multidisciplinary team in Gothenburg, Sweden, assessed 24 individuals with SRS. Age-appropriate cognitive assessments were performed and autistic traits were assessed using parental questionnaires and medical records. Perceptual visual dysfunctions (PVDs) were compared with 112 matched controls from a previous study in Gothenburg. The median age was 9.3 years (range 3.4-17.1) at the cognitive assessment and 11.7 years (range 3.4-22.1) at the ophthalmological examination. Intelligence quotient (IQ) scores ranged from 66-142 and 9/24 scored below 85. Verbal-performance IQ discrepancies of ≥15 points were observed in 12/22 individuals. Six boys reached the Autism Spectrum Screening Questionnaire cutoff scores or had an established autism spectrum disorder diagnosis. PVDs were recorded in 5/21 individuals and 4/112 controls (p = 0.008). There were 10/16 patients with abnormal VEPs: three had PVDs and four showed verbal-performance IQ discrepancies. Most individuals with SRS showed normal overall IQ, but neurodevelopmental concerns, impaired visual perception and abnormal VEPs were common. Regular follow-up visits are recommended.

title: Comprehensive Evaluation of an Adenine/Phosphate-Induced CKD Model for the Study of Aortic Valve Calcification.
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is prevalent in chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet no pharmacological therapies exist. Preclinical models rarely incorporate CKD-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD) features, limiting translational potential. We aimed to develop a comprehensive preclinical approach to study CKD-associated CAVD, suitable for standardized assessment of therapies on valvular, cardiac, vascular, and skeletal outcomes. Eight-week-old male Sprague Dawley rats were assigned to a control group (n=17) fed standard chow or an adenine-phosphate group (AP, n=21) fed chow supplemented with 0.3% adenine and 1.15% phosphate. Diets were enriched with 20% lactose and 19% casein to facilitate phosphate absorption and calcium solubility. Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography at baseline, week 5, and 9, with concurrent blood sampling. Aortic valve (AV) calcification was assessed by Alizarin Red and Osteosense staining, and aortic calcium quantified using O-Cresolphthalein Complexone. Gene expression in the aorta and left ventricle (LV) was analyzed by RNA-seq at week 9, and bone microarchitecture assessed by micro-CT. AP rats showed progressive increases in serum creatinine, calcium-phosphorus product, and uremic toxins. By week 9, they exhibited significant AV calcification, with reduced valve area and cusp separation. Relative wall thickness and LV histology were preserved, though transcriptomics revealed early priming toward inflammation and fibrosis. AP rats' aortas showed calcification, osteogenic features and reduced systolic expansion. Bone analysis revealed cortical thinning and increased porosity, while trabecular bone showed reduced trabecular number, increased trabecular spacing, and compensatory thickening. Together with elevated PTH and FGF23 levels, these changes suggest high bone turnover due to secondary hyperparathyroidism and are correlated with the extent of AV calcification. These results underscore the model's translational relevance, addressing multiple facets of CKD-MBD and supporting its use for preclinical screening of novel therapies targeting CKD-associated cardiovascular calcification.

title: RELAX Perinatal Digital Intervention to Prevent Increasing Anxiety: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Anxiety disorders affect 1 in 5 pregnant women and birthing people. Cognitive bias modification for interpretation reduces anxiety and repetitive negative thinking (RNT; a risk factor for anxiety) among nonpregnant samples. To evaluate whether adding pregnancy-tailored cognitive bias modification for interpretation to usual maternity care (UC) prevents increased anxiety during pregnancy; reduces anxiety, depression, and RNT before and after birth; and improves functioning before and after birth compared with UC. The RELAX (Reducing Levels of Anxiety) 2-arm, parallel-group, multisite, superiority, phase 2b randomized clinical trial recruited participants from June 2023 to July 2024, with final assessment in April 2025. Participants included pregnant individuals in the UK at 16 to 28 weeks' gestation, with high RNT and up to moderate anxiety, recruited via antenatal clinics or self-referral. Participants were randomized to the self-led digital intervention (RELAX plus UC), involving twelve 17-minute sessions over 4 weeks, or to UC. Assessments took place at baseline before randomization (T0) and 4 weeks (T1), 8 weeks (T2), and 36 weeks (T3; 12-24 weeks after birth) after randomization. The primary outcome was anxiety, as assessed by the 7-item Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale (GAD-7) at T2 and as a secondary outcome at T3. Secondary outcomes included RNT (assessed by the 10-item trait version of the Repetitive Thinking Questionnaire [RTQ-10]), depression (general and perinatal, assessed by the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 [PHQ-9] and Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale [EPDS]), perinatal anxiety (assessed by the Perinatal Anxiety Screening Scale [PASS]), worry (assessed by the Penn State Worry Questionnaire [PSWQ]), and functioning (assessed by the Work and Social Adjustment Scale [WSAS]). Interpretation bias at T1 was the hypothesized mechanism. Analysis was performed using a modified intention-to-treat approach. A total of 268 participants were randomized (mean [SD] age 33.7 [3.9] years; 174 [64.9%] married). Anxiety was significantly lower for RELAX participants vs UC (mean GAD-7 difference, -1.5; 95% CI, -2.4 to -0.6; P = .001). Depression (mean PHQ-9 difference, -0.8; 95% CI -1.5 to -0.1; and mean EPDS difference, -1.1; 95% CI, -2.0 to -0.2), RNT (mean RTQ-10 difference, -2.7; 95% CI, -4.5 to -0.9), worry (mean PSWQ difference, -3.6; 95% CI, -5.9 to -1.3), and perinatal anxiety (mean PASS difference, -5.5; 95% CI, -8.2 to -2.8) were significantly lower at T2. Effects on general anxiety (mean GAD-7 difference, -1.0; 95% CI, -1.9 to -0.1), postnatal depression (mean EPDS difference, -1.3; 95% CI, -2.4 to -0.2), and RNT (mean RTQ-10 difference, -2.4; 95% CI, -4.6 to -0.2) were sustained at T3. RELAX promoted more positive interpretations vs UC (mean difference, 2.1; 95% CI, 1.8-2.3) that did not mediate effects at T2 (indirect effect on GAD-7, -0.2; percentile bootstrap 95% CI, -0.4 to 0.1). Functioning did not differ at T2 (mean WSAS difference, -1.0; 95% CI, -2.5 to 0.5) or T3 (mean WSAS difference, -0.8; 95% CI, -2.7 to 1.2), nor did perinatal anxiety (mean PASS difference, -2.1; 95% CI, -5.5 to 1.4), general depression (mean PHQ-9 difference, -0.2; 95% CI, -1.2 to 0.9), or worry (mean PSWQ difference, -1.4; 95% CI, -4.1 to 1.3) at T3. In this randomized clinical trial, anxiety was lower during pregnancy and postnatally for RELAX plus UC participants compared with those receiving UC. Integrating RELAX into maternity care for those at risk of increased anxiety has potential to improve maternal mental health. https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN12754931.

title: The shared genetic architecture of the TDP-43 spectrum: Bridging clinical FTLD and neuropathological endophenotypes.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) proteinopathies encompass a spectrum of conditions including frontotemporal lobar degeneration with TDP-43 inclusions (FTLD-TDP), limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy (LATE-NC), and hippocampal sclerosis (HS). FTLD-TDP is further classified into several pathological subtypes (A, B, C, D, and E), which differ in the distribution and morphology of TDP-43 inclusions. Clinical and neuropathological variability across FTLD, FTLD-TDP, LATE-NC, and HS has hindered the translatability of genetic discoveries between clinical and pathological disease categories. By leveraging their genetic convergence, we aimed to refine effect size estimates and uncover variants that influence the TDP-43 spectrum. We conducted an inverse variance weighted fixed-effects meta-analysis using METAL, combining neuropathological datasets (FTLD-TDP subtypes: A [Ncases = 193], B [Ncases = 288], C [Ncases = 467], and controls [Ncontrols = 3153]), HS (Ncases = 751; Ncontrols = 6413), or LATE-NC (Ncases = 1325; Ncontrols = 1787). Additionally, we performed a random-effects meta-analysis that included clinically diagnosed FTLD (Ncases = 4685; Ncontrols = 15,308) and neuropathological datasets. Moreover, we performed colocalization, fine-mapping, and functional annotation analyses. Three loci reached genome-wide significance. The GRN (rs5848) and TMEM106B (rs3807865) loci were associated with FTLD-TDP (A and B), LATE-NC, and HS. Colocalization and fine-mapping analyses supported genetic signals at GRN and TMEM106B loci, while functional annotation suggested that rs3807865 and rs3807866 influence regulatory activity and TMEM106B expression in glial cells. MAPT demonstrated association across all combinations of TDP-43 proteinopathies (except FTLD-TDP B and C) and clinical FTLD, specifically the H1c haplotype. Our results extend the known role of GRN and TMEM106B beyond FTLD-TDP subtype A, while MAPT involvement suggests a role beyond traditional tauopathies.

title: Locus coeruleus microstructural integrity and sleep disruption in the context of Alzheimer's disease pathology.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: The locus coeruleus (LC) is among the first sites of tau pathology in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and plays a key role in sleep-wake regulation. However, evidence linking LC integrity to objective sleep measures in the context of emerging AD pathology remains limited. Thirty-nine cognitively unimpaired older adults underwent dedicated LC and neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging at 7T magnetic resonance imaging, actigraphy, and quantification of plasma AD-related biomarkers. A subsample of 20 individuals also completed at-home sleep electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings. Lower LC orientation dispersion index, indicating lower complexity in the arborization of LC neurites, was associated with actigraphy- and EEG-derived measures of shorter and more fragmented sleep. These associations were exacerbated at elevated plasma phosphorylated tau 217 and glial fibrillary acidic protein concentrations. Our findings provide in vivo evidence of the LC's involvement in sleep disruption, and they highlight LC microstructure as a potential marker for identifying individuals at risk for AD-related sleep disturbances.

title: Mind the route: different routes, different roles in descending motor pathways.
abstract: How are distinct descending motor pathways specified during development, and how do they contribute to movement? In a recent study, Kaiser et al. identified molecularly distinct cortical projection neurons that establish separate descending trajectories early in development. Their findings reveal a direct cortico-brainstem pathway with a specific role in skilled forelimb control, highlighting how developmental molecular identity can shape the functional organisation of descending motor circuits.

title: A tug-of-war in the niche: balancing forces to preserve stemness.
abstract: Stem cell niches are mechanically self-regulating systems. Segú Cristina and colleagues show that reciprocal adhesion between glial niche cells and neural stem cells buffers tensile forces, preserving nuclear and mitotic integrity and sustaining stem cell proliferation. They identify immunoglobulin complexes as critical mechanoregulators, linking adhesion, tissue mechanics, and stemness.

title: Reduced intracortical inhibition in hemiplegic migraine: An interictal transcranial magnetic stimulation study.
abstract: Neuronal hyperexcitability is thought to play a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of hemiplegic migraine (HM). Cortical excitability of the motor cortex can be evaluated using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS). However, previous interictal TMS studies have yielded contradictory results in HM patients. This retrospective cohort study characterized intracortical inhibitory and facilitatory networks in HM patients using TMS applied to the motor cortex. Single- and paired-pulse TMS paradigms were used to assess motor evoked potentials (MEP), cortical silent period (CSP), short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI), long-interval intracortical inhibition (LICI), and intracortical facilitation (ICF). Data were collected from 12 HM patients (8 female; mean age 32.3±11.3 years), including four with an ATP1A2 pathogenic variant, three with a SCN1A pathogenic variant, and five without an identified variant. Results were compared to normative reference data from 26 age- and sex-matched healthy participants assessed using the same TMS protocol. Between migraine attacks, HM patients exhibited a shorter CSP duration (median 72.8ms [IQR 49.9-122.1] vs. 107.8ms [IQR 98.2-128.4]; P=0.049) and decreased SICI (median ratio 111.8% [IQR 69.1-188.5] vs. 31.0% [IQR 18.2-54.4]; P<0.001) and LICI (median ratio 75.5% [IQR 26.8-98.9] vs. 15.0% [IQR 1.2-26.9]; P=0.012), indicating impaired inhibitory mechanisms. In contrast, ICF was not significantly different between groups (P=0.23). Two patients examined during an ongoing attack showed complete absence of MEPs from the affected hemisphere. These preliminary findings suggest that impaired cortical inhibition, reflected by reduced SICI and LICI, may contribute to the pathophysiology of HM. Conversely, intracortical facilitation (ICF) was not significantly altered with the present protocol. Replication in larger cohorts is needed.

title: Retinal computations.
Beyond Pathology: Perivascular Spaces as Dynamic Players in Neurodevelopment and Brain Health.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
abstract: Perivascular spaces (PVS) have historically been viewed as radiological markers of aging and cerebrovascular pathology. However, this narrow perspective overlooks accumulating evidence that PVS likely undergo dynamic, prolonged maturation across the lifespan and may play an essential role in healthy brain development. This Viewpoint article challenges the prevailing paradigm by positioning PVS not as passive anatomical structures or mere disease indicators, but as active participants in postnatal neurodevelopment whose morphology and function evolve to meet the metabolic and waste clearance demands of the maturing brain. We integrate evidence from advanced neuroimaging, developmental neuroscience, and neurobiology studies to highlight that PVS structure and fluid dynamics may be coupled with several neurodevelopmental processes, impacted by early experiences, and mature through adolescence to facilitate healthy brain development and cognitive functioning. We advocate for longitudinal, lifespan approaches to PVS research, because understanding normative PVS development is paramount for interpreting pathological changes. This developmental reframing highlights new opportunities for early identification of at-risk individuals and preventive interventions targeting the brain's waste clearance system during sensitive developmental windows.

title: A Stereotaxic Atlas of Primary Cortical Areas in the Developing Rat Brain from Postnatal Days 8 to 20.
abstract: Postnatal brain growth is nonlinear, making precise stereotaxic targeting in the developing rat neocortex difficult without age-specific knowledge of cortical area locations. Traditional atlases visualize brain slices in the coronal plane, which can obscure top-down areal boundaries and subdomains. To address these shortcomings, we created a developmental stereotaxic atlas that maps the neocortex of postnatal day (P) 8, P12, P16, and P20 in male and female Sprague Dawley and Long-Evans rats onto a coordinate grid. After using a stereotaxic device to create a grid of fluorescent probes, we extracted the brain, flattened neocortical tissue, and stained it for cytochrome oxidase, which is predominantly found in layer IV of primary cortical areas. Reconstructions of the primary somatosensory, auditory, and visual cortices demonstrate high structural reproducibility within each age and strain group. Our atlas captures the location of primary cortical areas at these four ages, showing that neocortical expansion is nonisometric, expanding preferentially along the rostral-caudal axis. Finally, we complement these top-down maps by extracting local neocortical surface angles from an existing coronal atlas, enabling proper electrode orientation to be perpendicular to the developing neocortex. Ultimately, this anatomically verified resource provides a standardized blueprint that eliminates resource-intensive trial-and-error mapping and maximizes experimental reproducibility in developmental systems neuroscience.

Predicting progression in Parkinson's disease.
