title: Further Extensive Evaluation of GHB-Pentose as a Novel Biomarker for the Extended Detection of GHB Intake/Administration in Forensic Casework.
abstract: Gamma-hydroxybutyrate (GHB) detection in forensic toxicology is hampered by its rapid elimination and endogenous occurrence. GHB-pentose has recently emerged as a promising biomarker capable of extending the detection window of GHB exposure but requires further evaluation in authentic forensic samples. We systematically investigated GHB-pentose using two independent LC-MS/MS methods based on hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC) and reversed-phase (RP) chromatography. Positive findings were evaluated against measured GHB concentrations, case information, matrix type, and concordance between analytical methods. Among 2414 urine cases, 97.6% were negative for GHB and GHB-pentose. GHB-pentose could be detected in all 21 GHB-positive urine samples from living individuals and in four GHB-positive postmortem cases, whereas 20 other postmortem urine samples with elevated GHB concentrations (10-26 mg/L) were negative for GHB-pentose. Based on toxicological expert assessment performed independently prior to this study, it was assumed that the GHB detected in these cases was more likely the result of postmortem formation than of prior GHB intake. Fourteen GHB-negative urine samples were positive for GHB-pentose; eight of these contained case information supporting previous GHB exposure, including three suspected drug-facilitated crimes sampled 13-16 h after the incident. GHB-pentose appears to be a highly specific biomarker of exogenous GHB exposure, capable of extending the detection window beyond that of GHB itself and potentially serving as a discriminant between exogenous GHB administration and endogenous, particularly postmortem, GHB formation. Routine LC-MS/MS screening is feasible, even in the absence of a reference standard, supporting its immediate implementation in forensic toxicology workflows.

title: Protective Role of Netrin-1 in the Female Nucleus Accumbens Following Amphetamine Exposure in Adolescence.
abstract: Adolescence is a period of mesocorticolimbic dopamine remodelling, when exposure to drugs of abuse can alter axon targeting and synaptic maturation. In adolescent male rodents, amphetamine causes dopamine axon mistargeting and long-term cognitive deficits via downregulation of the Netrin-1/DCC guidance system. In females, compensatory Netrin-1 protein upregulation in the nucleus accumbens protects against these effects. How Netrin-1 expression in the nucleus accumbens is regulated and what role it plays in local synaptic architecture remain unclear. Here, we mapped Netrin-1 mRNA (Ntn1) across development in nucleus accumbens medium spiny neurons, assessed the role of dopamine D1 and D2 receptor signalling in Netrin-1 protein expression and examined whether Netrin-1 maintains medium spiny neuron dendritic spine architecture following adolescent amphetamine exposure. We found that medium spiny neurons, particularly those co-expressing D1 and D2 receptors, were the principal source of Ntn1 mRNA in the nucleus accumbens in both sexes, with expression declining from early adolescence to adulthood. In adolescent females, systemic blockade of either D1 or D2 receptors reduced nucleus accumbens Netrin-1 protein levels under both baseline and amphetamine-exposed conditions. Although amphetamine did not alter Ntn1 mRNA in the nucleus accumbens, it increased its expression in the ventral tegmental area, suggesting a potential contribution from afferent projections. These findings indicate that Netrin-1 upregulation in adolescent females is dopamine-dependent and may protect against amphetamine-induced circuit disruption, possibly involving pre- and postsynaptic mechanisms.

title: Diacylglycerol kinase kappa is a target of the Prader-Willi syndrome gene SNORD116.
abstract: SNORD116 is a small nucleolar RNA deficient in Prader-Willi syndrome individuals. The mechanisms by which SNORD116 conveys its effects are unknown. Here, transcriptomic analysis showed that diacylglycerol kinase kappa (Dgkk) expression was elevated in the hypothalamus of Snord116-deficient mice. In silico analyses predicted a strong RNA:RNA interaction between Snord116 and Dgkk mRNA that is fully conserved in mouse and human. In vitro experiments in human cellular models demonstrated that SNORD116 mediates 2'-O-methylation of DGKK mRNA and regulates DGKK mRNA and protein expression. In Snord116-deficient mouse neurons, increased Dgkk expression was associated with attenuated diacylglycerol-mediated activation of ERK and PKC, critical elements in neuronal signaling cascades. In mice, brain Dgkk expression peaks during late embryonic and early postnatal periods, coinciding with peak rates of neurogenesis; its expression in adults is restricted mainly to brain regions implicated in Prader-Willi syndrome pathophysiology, including the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus. Fasting acutely decreased hypothalamic Dgkk expression in wild-type mice. Increased Dgkk expression in Snord116-deficient mice could reflect derangements in this pathway that affects both brain development and cell-specific functions.

title: Hypertension in Patients Receiving Maintenance Hemodialysis: Beyond Sodium and Dry Weight.
journal: Advances in kidney disease and health
abstract: Hypertension is highly prevalent in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis and is strongly associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Optimal strategies for diagnosis and management of hypertension are uncertain. Peridialysis blood pressure (BP) measurements, although critical for safety monitoring, are increasingly recognized as being unreliable for diagnosing hypertension or guiding therapy. Current evidence supports the use of 44-h ambulatory BP monitoring as the preferred diagnostic method, with home BP monitoring as a practical alternative. Out-of-office measurements correlate more closely with cardiovascular outcomes, left ventricular hypertrophy, and mortality than peridialysis readings. Despite observational data suggesting a linear association between higher out-of-dialysis BP and adverse outcomes, randomized controlled trials establishing definitive BP targets in dialysis patients are lacking. Both extremes of BP may confer harm, and aggressive BP lowering increases the risk of intradialytic hypotension and vascular access complications. Management should prioritize the optimization of volume status by attainment of dry weight and sodium restriction. If BP remains high, pharmacotherapy is indicated. Beta-blockers are generally favored as first-line agents given their antihypertensive efficacy and potential cardiovascular benefits. Future research should focus on the role of emerging cardiovascular therapies, large-scale clinical trials to establish appropriate BP targets, and real-world implementation of out-of-office BP measurements.

title: "Neuroplasticity and neuroimmune interactions with type 2 inflammation in asthma." C.S. Koster, C. Lavitola, R. Teodorescu, et al. Eur Respir Rev 2026; 35: 250159.
journal: European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society

title: Tumor-nervous system crosstalk in PDAC: Current landscape, challenges, and future directions.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most lethal and treatment-refractory malignancies worldwide, largely driven by its uniquely desmoplastic and highly innervated microenvironment. Given the striking incidence of perineural invasion and its profound correlation with intractable cancer pain and early recurrence, tumor-nervous system crosstalk has emerged as a pivotal driver of PDAC progression. Neural components-including neurotransmitters, neurotrophic factors, axon guidance molecules, and specific sensory and autonomic networks (e.g., dorsal root ganglia and sympathetic nerves)-do not merely act as passive conduits, but actively orchestrate tumor genesis, metastasis, and immune evasion. Crucially, this neuro-stromal crosstalk actively drives chemoresistance by facilitating the dual-effect remodeling of tumor energy metabolism and detoxification networks. In this comprehensive review, we decode the multidimensional molecular mechanisms and reciprocal signaling cascades underpinning tumor-nervous system crosstalk. We critically evaluate the translational challenges of applying neurotherapy in clinical practice, encompassing mechanistic pleiotropy, neural plasticity, and visceral safety risks. Furthermore, by synthesizing emerging clinical trials targeting neurotransmitter axes, dorsal root ganglia, and neurotrophic signaling, we provide a forward-looking roadmap for integrating precision neuro-oncology with standard regimens to simultaneously alleviate cancer pain and overcome therapeutic resistance in PDAC.

title: Human immunodeficiency virus 1 glycoprotein Gp120 induces amyloid pathology in neurons.
abstract: The neuropathology of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-associated neurocognitive disorder (HAND) brains is similar to Alzheimer's disease brains in terms of an accumulation of the neurotoxic amyloid beta (Aβ) peptide. To test this hypothesis, we measured the levels of amyloid precursor protein (APP) and Aβ in HAND cerebrospinal fluid. We observed a 2-fold reduction in APP levels contrasted by an increase in Aβ in people living with HIV. However, the mechanism underlying these effects is challenging to elucidate. HIV may exert its neurotoxic effects in the CNS through the actions of the envelope glycoprotein gp120. Therefore, we exposed rat cortical neurons to this envelope protein. Neurons exposed to gp20 exhibited a morphological pathology as well as a 2-fold increase in the cellular levels of APP and Aβ42. The effect of gp120 was blocked by AMD3100, a CXCR4 antagonist. We then determined APP and Aβ levels in the hippocampus of aged gp120-transgenic (tg) mice, an animal model of HAND. Gp120 transgenic animals also exhibit a ~2-fold increase in APP and Aβ42 levels compared to wild type (WT). There was no change in APP mRNA, suggesting that the increase in Aβ42 could be due to APP processing. We then measured the hippocampal levels of beta-site APP cleaving enzyme-1 (BACE-1), and presenilin 1 and 2, nicastrin, and anterior pharynx defective 1 (APH1), components of the gamma secretase complex, in WT and gp120tg mice. We observed no significant changes in BACE1 levels; however, presenilin 1 levels were significantly increased, whereas nicastrin levels were significantly decreased in gp120 tg mice. Together, our data suggest that gp120 may be an important mechanism contributing to Aβ accumulation in HAND. This research advances our understanding of the mechanisms contributing to HAND, and establishes a novel mechanism for gp120 neurotoxicity involving the production of toxic protein.

title: High-frequency rTMS improves post-stroke cognitive impairment and is associated with region-specific BBB remodeling and increased pericyte coverage.
abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) remains without effective disease-modifying therapies. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) is a promising noninvasive intervention, but whether its beneficial effects are associated with blood-brain barrier (BBB) remodeling and pericyte coverage remains unclear. In this study, adult male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) or sham surgery. Beginning on post-operative day 7, tMCAO rats received either restraint-only handling or 20-Hz rTMS once daily for 21 consecutive days. Behavioral performance, cerebral blood flow (CBF), infarct volume, BBB leakage, and vascular remodeling were evaluated using behavioral tests, laser speckle imaging, TTC staining, immunofluorescence, and Western blotting. High-frequency rTMS improved cognitive performance and reduced anxiety-like behavior after stroke. These behavioral benefits were accompanied by increased ipsilateral CBF, although infarct volume was not significantly reduced. Moreover, rTMS was associated with partial, region-specific BBB remodeling, including reduced cortical IgG leakage, increased vascular Occludin expression, and enhanced pericyte coverage, particularly in the hippocampus. Evans blue extravasation showed a nonsignificant trend toward reduction. In conclusion, subacute high-frequency rTMS improved behavioral outcomes after stroke and was associated with region-specific BBB remodeling and increased pericyte coverage. These findings suggest that vascular and perivascular remodeling may contribute to the beneficial effects of rTMS in PSCI.

title: Positive regulation of astrocytic sonic hedgehog expression through TRPV4-mediated ERK and NF-κB signaling pathway as a protective mechanism against traumatic brain injury.
abstract: Sonic hedgehog (Shh) is a secreted protein that plays important roles in neuronal and vascular protection. Although Shh expression increases in astrocytes following traumatic brain injury (TBI), the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the mechanisms responsible for TBI-induced Shh expression and its functional significance. Fluid percussion injury (FPI) was performed to establish in vitro and in vivo TBI models. In cultured astrocytes, FPI increased Shh mRNA expression and protein levels, as determined by real-time PCR and enzyme immunoassay. Pharmacological antagonists (HC-067047 and RN-1734) or siRNA-mediated knockdown of transient receptor potential vanilloid 4 (TRPV4) suppressed this increase. Furthermore, inhibitors of calcium, protein kinase C (PKC), extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), and nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) attenuated Shh expression induced by FPI or the TRPV4 agonist (GSK1016790A). In TBI model mice, immunohistochemical observation found that Shh expression was predominantly observed in astrocytes. FPI increased Shh mRNA expression and protein levels in the mouse cerebrum, whereas repeated intraventricular administration of TRPV4 antagonists, inhibitors of calcium, PKC, ERK, and NF-κB suppressed these increases. Evans blue extravasation assay and rotarod test demonstrated that TRPV4 antagonist treatment impaired recovery of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption and motor dysfunction in mice following FPI, respectively. Shh treatment reversed these adverse effects, suggesting that Shh contributes to functional recovery after TBI. In conclusion, Shh expression is promoted through the TRPV4-mediated calcium/PKC/ERK/NF-κB signaling pathway in astrocytes and astrocytic Shh may play protective roles in TBI by supporting BBB integrity and neurological recovery.

title: Seizure susceptibility following a single acute cluster of cortical spreading depolarizations in a rat model of traumatic brain injury.
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major risk factor for acquired epilepsy, yet the acute pathophysiologic events contributing to post-traumatic epileptogenesis remain poorly understood. Cortical spreading depolarizations (CSDs) occur in up to 60% of moderate-to-severe TBI patients and impose substantial metabolic and neurovascular stress on the injured brain, but their contribution to post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) is unknown. We investigated whether acute repetitive CSDs influence epileptogenesis following experimental TBI. Adult male Sprague Dawley rats underwent a lateral fluid percussion or sham injury followed by 2 h of KCl-induced CSDs. Animals survived for 6 months with video electroencephalographic monitoring for spontaneous seizures, followed by pentylenetetrazol (PTZ) seizure susceptibility testing and histologic evaluation of hippocampal markers. Spontaneous seizures occurred in 14% of TBI animals, but we did not identify significant interaction effects of TBI and CSDs. However, TBI and TBI + CSD animals experienced seizures with increased electrographic intensity in comparison to sham animals (p = 0.0194 and p = 0.0054, respectively). No significant differences were observed in hippocampal volume (2-way ANOVA, p = 0.285), or parvalbumin (p = 0.689) or calretinin (p = 0.848) immunopositivity. In contrast, CSDs were associated with decreased zinc transporter 3 (ZnT3) immunopositivity in the hippocampal hilus (p = 0.025). These findings suggest that a single acute cluster of CSDs can promote neuronal hypersynchrony and molecular adaptations in the hippocampus, despite not significantly increasing seizure incidence. Together, our findings provide initial evidence that CSDs may modify features associated with epileptogenesis and warrant further investigation of whether greater, more prolonged CSD burdens, as observed clinically after TBI, contribute to the development of PTE.

title: From metabolic dysfunction to neurodegeneration: mechanisms and hierarchical candidate biomarkers in diabetes-associated cognitive impairment.
abstract: Diabetes-associated cognitive impairment (DACI) is a common complication of diabetes that severely affects patients' quality of life. However, biomarkers for its clinical diagnosis and treatment remain limited. DACI pathogenesis involves hyperglycemia, advanced glycation end products (AGE)-receptor for AGE interactions, insulin resistance, and lipid metabolism disorders, which induce oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroinflammation. Neurons, microglia, and astrocytes are key cellular mediators. Metabolic disorders directly impair neuronal energy metabolism, synaptic plasticity, and neurogenesis, while microglial activation and functional reprogramming, astrocytic lipid synthesis, and synaptic remodeling further promote neuronal dysfunction and cognitive decline. This review distinguishes clinically investigated biomarkers from genetic susceptibility factors, emerging mechanistic candidates, evaluates them by evidence level and potential clinical roles in risk assessment, diagnosis, disease monitoring, treatment-response assessment, and therapeutic targeting. Integrating mechanistic and biomarker evidence provides a framework for future research, early diagnosis, and targeted therapeutic development. However, many candidate biomarkers have been investigated primarily in preclinical models or related diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and require systematic validation in well-characterized human DACI cohorts.

title: HIV-1 Tat drives genotype-dependent neuroimmune programs that promote Parkinson Disease-like neurodegeneration in the hSNCAA53TGba1 mouse model.
abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus type I (HIV-1) infection can induce both motor and cognitive impairments even in patients receiving combination antiretroviral therapy (cART). These neurological alterations are related to direct and indirect mechanisms represented by viral and immune mediated processes, respectively. HIV-1 directly elicits neurological damages through some viral proteins including transactivator of transcription (Tat), a protein involved in the HIV-1 replication and able to affect neural cell through autocrine and paracrine pathways. In this study, we investigated the functional and transcriptional effects of intrastriatal Tat injection in pre-symptomatic mice carrying the hSNCAA53TGba1+/+ and hSNCAA53TGba1+/L444P mutations, common genetic risk factors for Parkinson's disease (PD). Behavioural assessment revealed that Tat administration anticipated motor symptoms onset in both genotypes, with some behavioural measures suggesting greater impairment in mice carrying both mutations, whereas spatial memory was not affected. In line with these findings, Tat injection induced significant loss of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH)-positive cells and fibre density in hSNCAA53TGba1+/L444P mice. HIV-1 Tat injection did not significantly modify TH-positive fibre density in hSNCAA53TGba1+/+ mice, whereas a marked reduction was observed in hSNCAA53TGba1+/L444P mice. Transcriptomic analysis revealed genotype-dependent responses, with a predominant innate immune-related signatures in hSNCAA53TGba1+/+ mice and transcriptional alterations involving immune, lysosomal, proteostatic, and autophagy-related pathways hSNCAA53TGba1+/L444P mice mice. Altogether, these findings indicate that HIV-1 Tat administration is associated with genotype-dependent PD-related motor deficits and that the Gba1 deficiency is linked to a more pronounced dopaminergic and transcriptional response to Tat exposure.

title: Caloric restriction and intermittent fasting initiated during lactation alter maternal behaviour and amygdalar redox status in dams.
abstract: The lactational period requires substantial metabolic and behavioural adaptations, and more than 70% of mothers report weight concerns and attempt weight loss by four months postpartum. Nevertheless, how distinct restrictive paradigms initiated during lactation alter maternal behaviour, and the extent to which associated neurochemical changes relate to these behaviours, remains poorly understood. In the current study, we modeled restrictive diets in lactating rats to evaluate caregiving behaviour and its relationship to amygdalar redox status. Intermittent fasting (IF) and caloric restriction (CR) were administered to lactating Wistar dams from postpartum day 0 to day 28, and impaired maternal care, evidenced by delayed pup retrieval and decreased nursing frequency relative to ad libitum-fed controls. Both diets reduced body and adipose tissue weight, and energy efficiency. IF and CR increased impulsivity-like phenotype: CR doubled open-arm exploration in the elevated plus maze; IF and CR increased center-zone exploration in the open field by three- and two-fold, respectively; IF doubled time spent in the light chamber of the light-dark box. A composite behavioural score showed impairment in dams in both IF and CR groups. At the neurochemical level, both diets reduced amygdalar superoxide dismutase activity, which correlated negatively with the composite behavioural score. Both restrictive diets produced an underweight phenotype with weakened dam-pup interactions and an impulsivity-like response. These behavioural changes co-occurred with amygdalar redox imbalance, which correlated with the severity of the behavioural score. Overall, the study refines understanding of the nutritional and behavioural consequences of dietary restriction initiated during lactation and identifies disrupted redox homeostasis as a candidate mechanism.

title: DNA methylation remodeling across adulthood in the rhesus macaque hippocampus.
abstract: DNA methylation (DNAm) is a key epigenetic mechanism implicated in brain aging, yet methylation trajectories across the lifespan in the primate brain remain poorly understood. To characterize age-associated DNAm patterns in the hippocampus, we generated reduced representation bisulfite sequencing (RRBS) data from 86 rhesus macaque hippocampus samples spanning ~3-35 years of age (females = 56; males = 30). CpG-level analyses revealed minimal age-associated changes in mean methylation, with sites trending toward intermediate states, but widespread increases in methylation variability, consistent with epigenetic drift and reduced regulatory fidelity. Region-level modeling identified 5163 age-associated methylation regions exhibiting both monotonic and nonlinear trajectories across age. Nonlinear clusters revealed midlife inflections centered around 12.3 and 13.2 years, suggesting that hippocampal epigenetic aging may involve molecular transition periods that shape later-life brain aging trajectories. Integration of these age-associated DNAm regions with matched RNAseq data identified candidate cis-regulatory loci where age-associated methylation may be linked to transcriptional changes, including IGF1R. In addition, direct testing of associations between mean gene methylation and expression revealed a significant repressive directional bias (higher methylation associated with lower expression) highlighting genes involved in neuroinflammation, amyloid processing, and myelin maintenance. Intergenic regions overlapped annotated human brain enhancers, indicating that age-associated methylation remodeling extends to distal cis-regulatory elements. Together, these findings indicate that hippocampal DNAm aging in a long-lived primate is dominated by increasing epigenetic variability at the CpG level alongside regional remodeling of both genic and intergenic regulatory loci, with potential implications for transcriptional remodeling during brain aging.

title: Traumatic childhood events and higher risk of major depressive disorder: The non-moderating role of sex.
abstract: Traumatic childhood events have been associated with poorer adult mental health. We examined associations between childhood trauma subtypes and current and lifetime major depressive disorder (MDD), and assessed sex moderation on these associations. From the Lifelines population-based cohort (Netherlands; mean age 47.5 ± 12.7; 59.1% female), we used analytic samples comprising 60,815 participants for current MDD and 42,375 for lifetime MDD. Trauma was assessed with the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ; total score and five subtypes). MDD was determined via the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview and the Lifetime Depression Assessment Self-Report. Logistic regression models were adjusted for sociodemographic and lifestyle covariates. Differences between subtypes were evaluated by effect-size magnitude, with FDR correction. Sex-by-trauma interactions and sex differences were tested. Current MDD prevalence was 4.3%, lifetime MDD 22.9%. Higher total CTQ score was associated with greater odds of current (OR = 1.64; 95%CI 1.59,1.69) and lifetime (OR = 1.55; 95%CI 1.52,1.59) MDD. All subtypes were associated with both outcomes; emotional neglect and abuse showed the strongest associations, meaningfully stronger than physical and sexual abuse but similar to each other. Sex largely did not moderate these associations, except for a stronger association between sexual abuse and lifetime MDD in males. Females showed higher rates of both MDD outcomes. Total CTQ scores did not meaningfully differ by sex, but females reported higher emotional abuse and sexual abuse scores. All childhood trauma subtypes were independently associated with MDD, with emotional trauma showing the strongest associations. Largely absent sex moderation, alongside females' higher exposure to emotional and sexual abuse and higher depression prevalence, suggests the sex gap in depression may reflect differential exposure rather than differential vulnerability to trauma.

title: Statin use and depression in older adults: a target trial emulation with implication for prevention and long-term management.
abstract: Late-life depression is one of the most common mental disorders, with limited response to antidepressant therapy. Statins, widely used for CVD, may influence depression risk through pleiotropic effects, though evidence remains inconclusive. This study evaluated the association between statin use and depression in older adults, assessing both prevention and management, effect modification by low-grade inflammation, and polygenic risk score (PGS), and statin safety. We used data from the ASPirin in Reducing Events in the Elderly (ASPREE) trial and its extended follow up, aged ≥70 years (≥65 years for US minorities) followed for a median of 8.4 years. We investigated whether statin use was associated with a lower risk of depressive symptom occurrence (prevention) and improved existing depression (long-term management). To address these distinct research questions, two analytic cohorts were defined at time zero (T0): individuals without depression and those with pre-existing depression, respectively. We emulated trial using a prespecified protocol and inverse probability treatment weighting were used to address confounding. The study included 17,231 participants without and 3478 with depression at time zero. Statin use was associated with a lower risk of depression (RR, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.76-0.84), irrespective of statin lipophilicity among those without depression at T0. Preventive associations strengthened with higher PGS, depression severity, and treatment duration. No significant association was observed in existing depression cohort; while protective association was observed in higher PGS (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.73-0.95). No evidence of long-term statin hepatic safety concerns was observed. Findings were robust across sensitivity analyses. Statin use was associated with a lower risk of depressive symptoms among those without depression at T0, but not among those with existing depression regardless of lipophilicity. Associations were stronger among individuals with higher genetic susceptibility to depression but showed no evidence of modification low-grade inflammation. Residual confounding cannot be excluded, and confirmation in future RCTs is warranted.

title: Pushing the Boundaries with Endo-aortic Intervention: Is Total Endovascular Aortic Repair Niche or Next Frontier?
journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

title: Chasing the ideal lumen thought lesion preparation: Lessons from the BALI trial on calcified lesions.
Brain-derived neurotrophic factor in gynecological cancers and endometriosis: A candidate biomarker for diagnosis and disease monitoring.
journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
abstract: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), a member of the neurotrophin family, has functions beyond neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity, including the regulation of cellular proliferation, migration, angiogenesis, inflammation, and nociceptive signaling. Growing evidence suggests that abnormal BDNF expression and dysregulated BDNF/TrkB signaling may contribute to the development and progression of gynecological malignancies, including ovarian, cervical, and endometrial cancers, as well as endometriosis. In cancer, BDNF has been associated with epithelial-mesenchymal transition, anoikis resistance, metastatic spread, and therapeutic resistance through PI3K/Akt, MAPK/ERK, and PLCγ signaling. In endometriosis, increased circulating and tissue BDNF has been associated with neuroangiogenesis, pelvic pain, lesion severity, and inflammatory remodeling. Emerging clinical and translational evidence suggests that BDNF may have potential as a minimally invasive biomarker, mainly in endometriosis, whereas clinical data in gynecological cancers come largely from tissue expression studies; however, associations between circulating BDNF levels and disease presence, severity, or treatment response remain heterogeneous across studies. The review is based on searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science from database inception to June 2025. This review critically synthesizes the molecular mechanisms underlying BDNF dysregulation and its interactions with hormonal, immune, and epigenetic pathways, while evaluating its potential clinical utility for diagnosis and disease monitoring. Particular emphasis is placed on methodological limitations, contradictory findings, and factors that may contribute to variability among studies. Key knowledge gaps and future research priorities, including standardized measurement approaches, prospective investigations, and independent cohort validation, are also discussed. Overall, current evidence supports further investigation of BDNF as a candidate biomarker, but its diagnostic and disease-monitoring utility has not been established and requires prospective clinical validation.

title: Effects of environmental enrichment and social isolation in preclinical rodent models: role of the endocannabinoid system.
abstract: Environmental enrichment (EE) and social isolation (SI) represent contrasting forms of environmental manipulation that differentially engage homeostatic mechanisms and exert profound effects on brain function, behaviour, and health. Both EE and SI have been shown to modulate the endocannabinoid (EC) system, a key lipid signalling system involved in maintaining homeostasis and regulating diverse physiological and pathological processes. This review provides an overview of preclinical animal studies investigating the role of the EC system in the effects of EE and SI. The available evidence indicates that both EE and SI significantly alter EC signalling, with EE most commonly associated with increased CB1 receptor expression, whereas SI is associated with disrupted CB1 receptor functionality and dysregulated EC signalling. These effects are region-specific, influenced by the type and duration of environmental manipulation, developmental stage, underlying pathology and possibly sex. Pharmacological and genetic manipulation studies further implicate CB1 receptor signalling in mediating some of the beneficial effects of EE and reduced CB1 signalling in the detrimental consequences of SI on behaviour. Overall, the findings support a role for the EC system as an important mediator through which EE and SI modulate neural plasticity and behavioural outcomes. Further mechanistic and translational studies, including both sexes and relevant disease models, are needed to determine how these mechanisms may inform future prevention and treatment strategies.

title: Association between functional connectome features and circulating amino acid levels in early-stage Parkinson's disease: An exploratory study.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by early alterations in large-scale brain functional connectivity and possible disturbances in excitatory amino acid metabolism. However, it is unknown whether topological changes in functional connectome reflect disruptions in the homeostasis of circulating glutamate and aspartate levels. Resting-state fMRI and High-Performance Liquid Chromatography are used to correlate brain and blood measures in 74 early-stage PD patients (mean age ± s.d. 63.5 ± 8.6 years, 51 males, 37 drug-naïve) and 20 healthy control (HC) volunteers (mean age ± s.d. 60.2 ± 5.6, 11 males). PD-relevant graph-theoretical metrics of fMRI connectomes are co-varied to serum-levels of N-Methyl-d-aspartate receptor (NMDAR)-related (L-/D-) amino acids (including precursors and related ratios). In male PD patients, compared to sex-matched HC subjects, strength of cortical sensorimotor nodes and clustering of subcortical nodes negatively correlate to D-/total aspartate ratio; clustering of temporal nodes positively correlates to l-aspartate; global characteristic path length negatively correlates to L-glutamate. Enlarging the panel of L-amino acids, l-serine markedly predicts metrics in treated male PD patients. Peripheral balance of excitatory amino acids and their precursors appear linked to large-scale brain network (re)organization in early-stage PD, supporting the potential value of these neuroactive biomolecules as circulating markers of functional brain integrity.

title: GABAergic regulation of reproduction in teleost fishes: An integrative neuroendocrine perspective.
abstract: γ-Aminobutyric acid (GABA) is the principal inhibitory neurotransmitter in the vertebrate central nervous system and an important regulator of reproductive neuroendocrine function. Over four decades, evidence has demonstrated receptor-specific actions of GABA at multiple levels of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis, yet knowledge of its role in teleost reproduction remains dispersed across neuroanatomical, pharmacological, physiological and molecular studies. This review synthesizes current knowledge of the teleost GABAergic system and its central and peripheral roles in regulating gonadotropin-releasing hormone neuronal activity, pituitary gonadotropin secretion, gonadal steroidogenesis, gametogenesis and puberty. GABAergic effects vary with receptor subtype, species, sex, developmental stage and endocrine state. Recent studies in viviparous teleosts further suggest a role for GABAergic signalling in the interaction between the hypothalamic-pituitary-interrenal and HPG axes. Finally, major knowledge gaps are identified and future research directions are proposed to advance mechanistic and comparative studies of GABAergic regulation of reproduction across vertebrates.

title: BMP2 and BMP6 prodomains are essential to generate heterodimers in liver endothelial cells and associate with ligands after cleavage and secretion.
abstract: Liver endothelial cell (LEC)-derived bone morphogenetic proteins (BMP)2 and BMP6 coordinately regulate hepatocyte hepcidin production to control systemic iron homeostasis, but the mechanisms are uncertain. BMPs are homodimeric or heterodimeric proteins that are generated as precursors comprised of a non-signaling prodomain and an active ligand released by proteolytic cleavage. Although prodomains do not signal, they play pleiotropic roles in ligand generation and activity. Here, we used LEC- and hepatocyte-derived cell cultures to explore how BMP2 and BMP6 prodomains and proteolytic cleavage impact homodimer formation, heterodimer formation, and hepcidin regulation. We show that when co-expressed in LECs, BMP2 and BMP6 form heterodimers, which more potently induce hepcidin versus homodimers. Proteolytic cleavage of BMP2 precursors at two furin consensus sites is required to generate fully active BMP2/6 heterodimers, although cleavage at either site generates partially active heterodimers. Uncleavable BMP6 precursors fail to generate fully active BMP2/6 heterodimers and dominant negatively inhibit BMP2 homodimer formation. We also show that in LECs, cognate BMP2 and BMP6 prodomains are essential for homodimer and heterodimer formation. Finally, both prodomains remain noncovalently associated with BMP2/6 heterodimers after cleavage and secretion. BMP6 prodomains also remain associated with BMP6 homodimers, whereas the association of BMP2 prodomains with BMP2 homodimers is influenced by the presence of the linker region between the cleavage sites. Our findings suggest that BMP2/6 heterodimers are likely the primary endogenous ligand that regulates hepcidin and iron homeostasis, and both BMP2 and BMP6 prodomains are critical to functional BMP2/6 formation in LECs.

title: Long-Term Structural Stability and Maturation of Centimeter-Scale Stretch-Grown Sensory Axons Following Collagen Encapsulation.
abstract: Peripheral nerve injury (PNI) remains a significant clinical challenge due to limited biologically active regeneration strategies. Tissue engineered nerve grafts (TENGs) comprising long-projecting, stretch-grown axon tracts have emerged as a promising strategy to guide regeneration by creating a living bridge guiding and aiding native regeneration processes. However, their long-term structural stability remains incompletely understood. In this study, we evaluated the effects of dorsal root ganglia (DRG) plating density on the structural stability and morphology of mechanically stretch-grown TENGs over 5-7 weeks after three-dimensional collagen-encapsulation and removal from the mechanobioreactor. TENGs generated from 20, 40, or 80 DRG maintained neuronal-axonal phenotype and exhibited robust longitudinal axonal alignment across all conditions. While higher-density TENGs demonstrated a modest but significant reduction in length over time, overall contraction remained limited, and contraction rates were not significantly different among the groups. Stretch-grown axons maintained over 90% of their immediate post-stretch length out to 5-7 weeks post-encapsulation. Higher density TENGs also exhibited increased integration and fusion of DRG, forming continuous neuronal somatic fields and the ends of the TENGs and running perpendicular to the stretch-grown axons. Moreover, quantitative analyses revealed density- and time-dependent remodeling of axonal fascicular architecture, characterized by increased fascicle diameter without substantial changes in fascicle number, consistent with progressive axonal thickening, bundling and network consolidation. Despite this maturation-associated remodeling, TENGs preserved overall structural integrity and alignment through 7 weeks in culture. Collectively, these findings establish TENGs as mechanically stable, dynamically remodeling tissues and support their potential use as nerve repair strategies requiring graft stability over clinically relevant timeframes. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Tissue-engineered nerve grafts (TENGs) use living, stretch-grown axons to guide repair after peripheral nerve injury, but their long-term structural stability has remained unclear. In this study, we show that collagen-encapsulated TENGs generated with different dorsal root ganglia densities remain intact for up to seven weeks, preserve longitudinal axon alignment, and retain more than 90% of their original length. At the same time, their internal architecture continues to mature through axon bundling and fascicle thickening, particularly at higher cell densities. These findings establish that TENGs can undergo biological remodeling without losing overall shape or dimensions. This "dynamic stability" is important for reproducible manufacturing, storage, surgical handling, and future translation of living nerve grafts for peripheral nerve repair.

title: First- and second-generation antipsychotic use in pregnancy and risks of pregnancy and birth outcomes.
journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
abstract: Antipsychotic use in pregnancy has increased, but evidence on potential maternal and neonatal complications remains limited. To evaluate the associations between continued first-generation antipsychotic (FG) or second-generation antipsychotic (SG) use during pregnancy and the risks of pregnancy complications and adverse birth outcomes. We conducted a population-based cohort study including all liveborn singletons born to women in Denmark (2004-2022) who filled ≥1 antipsychotic prescription from one year to 30 days before conception. Women who continued FGs or SGs through 20 gestational weeks (for pregnancy complications) or throughout pregnancy (for birth outcomes) were classified as continuers. SGs were further categorized into high metabolic risk (olanzapine, quetiapine, clozapine) or low metabolic risk (risperidone, aripiprazole, ziprasidone). Outcomes included gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, and adverse birth outcomes identified from medical records. Adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were estimated using generalized estimating equations, accounting for maternal characteristics and psychiatric history. Among 7,417 pregnancies, 453 (6.1%) were exposed to FGs, 2,219 (29.9%) to SGs, and 4,745 discontinued treatment. Compared with their respective discontinuers, continuing SGs was associated with higher odds of gestational diabetes (OR = 1.19, 95% CI 0.96-1.48) and gestational hypertension (OR = 1.20, 95% CI 0.97-1.48), whereas no increased risk was observed for FGs (OR = 0.92, 95% CI 0.57-1.48 and OR = 1.01, 95% CI 0.60-1.71, respectively). Risks were similar for high- and low-metabolic risk SGs for gestational diabetes, whereas the increased risk of gestational hypertension was confined to high-metabolic risk SGs. Preterm birth was less common among SG continuers (OR = 0.77, 95% CI 0.64-0.93), but not among FG continuers (OR = 1.13, 95% CI 0.80-1.60). Neonatal intensive care unit admission was more frequent among FG continuers (OR = 1.28, 95% CI 1.01-1.62), but not among SG continuers (OR = 0.87, 95% CI 0.73-1.03). Continuation of FGs during pregnancy was not associated with increased maternal risk but was associated with higher rates of neonatal intensive care admission, compared with discontinuation. Continuation of SGs was associated with increased maternal metabolic risk and a lower risk of preterm birth.

title: MRI-BASED BIPLANAR PREDICTION OF THE DOMINANT FACIAL NERVE PLANE IN BENIGN PAROTID SURGERY USING FIXED OSSEOUS LANDMARKS.
journal: Journal of stomatology, oral and maxillofacial surgery
abstract: Preservation of the facial nerve remains the principal technical challenge in benign parotid surgery. Conventional superficial-versus-deep classification does not predict whether the dominant nerve plane will be encountered over or deep to the tumor. This study evaluated an MRI-based biplanar model anchored to fixed osseous landmarks. Adults undergoing surgery for benign parotid neoplasms between January 2010 and December 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Operative findings were the reference standard. Axial deep displacement (ADD), coronal medial offset (CMO), axial posterior proximity, maximum tumor diameter, and cranio-caudal level were assessed. A prespecified logistic model incorporating ADD, CMO, and cranio-caudal level was developed in the 2010-2021 cohort, internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples, and temporally validated in the 2022-2025 cohort. Of 482 screened cases, 217 were eligible; 124 (57.1%) had an overlying/superior-superficial plane and 93 (42.9%) a deep/inferomedial plane. In a 50-case subset, interobserver agreement was excellent for ADD (ICC 0.941), CMO (ICC 0.965), and cranio-caudal level (weighted κ 0.908). The apparent derivation AUC was 0.849 and the optimism-corrected AUC 0.842. Temporal validation in 52 patients (33 events) yielded an AUC of 0.877 (95% CI 0.777-0.958) and a Brier score of 0.153. Calibration could be estimated only imprecisely (intercept 0.491, 95% CI -0.191 to 1.172; slope 1.173, 95% CI 0.522 to 1.824), and the validation results are therefore preliminary. Zone A predicted an overlying plane in 91.7% of cases, whereas Zone C predicted a deep plane in 81.0%. A biplanar MRI model based on fixed osseous landmarks provides a reproducible estimate of the dominant facial nerve plane from routine MRI. Discrimination was preserved on temporal validation, whereas calibration remains imprecisely estimated; external validation and prospective evaluation of clinical utility are required before clinical implementation.

title: Vicatia thibetica H. Boissieu: An ethnopharmacological review of botany, phytochemistry, traditional uses, pharmacological activities, safety, quality control, and applications.
abstract: The dried root of Vicatia thibetica H. Boissieu (VTR) is an ethnomedicinal and medicinal-food resource traditionally used in Tibetan medicine, Bai folk medicine, and regional dietary practices in southwestern China. Traditionally, VTR has been used as a tonic and dietary medicine for relieving fatigue, regulating menstruation, and alleviating gastrointestinal and cold-dampness-related disorders. Despite its long history of use and potential applications in functional foods and traditional compound preparations, current evidence regarding its active constituents, pharmacological mechanisms, quality control strategies, and safety remains incomplete and requires systematic validation. This review aims to critically evaluate the ethnopharmacological evidence supporting the traditional use and rational development of VTR. By integrating Tibetan medical records, Bai folk medicinal practices, regional materia medica, modern dietary uses, phytochemical reports, pharmacological studies, safety data, quality-control evidence, and patent-based applications, this review focuses on the source traceability of traditional uses, the distinction between the botanical species and the medicinal material, the reliability of chemical identification, the evidence level of pharmacological findings, and the major gaps that currently limit quality standardization, safety evaluation, and product development of VTR. A comprehensive literature survey on VTR was conducted to collect and evaluate traditional uses, botany, phytochemistry, pharmacological activities, toxicity and safety evaluation, quality control, and patent-based applications. Relevant studies and application-related records were retrieved from major international and Chinese databases and academic search platforms, including Web of Science, PubMed, Google Scholar, SciFinder, X-MOL, Baidu Scholar, CNKI, and Wanfang Data, covering records available from database inception to June 18, 2026. Patent information was retrieved from the China Patent Retrieval System (CPRS) and the CNKI patent database. Searches were performed using Boolean operators (AND/OR) with core plant and medicinal material terms, including "Vicatia thibetica", "Vicatia thibetica H. Boissieu", "Vicatia thibetica de Boiss.", "Xigui", "Jiawa", "Saigui", "" and "", combined with topic terms such as "traditional use", "ethnopharmacology", "Tibetan medicine", "Bai medicine", "botany", "phytochemistry", "chemical constituent", "pharmacology", "toxicity", "safety evaluation", "quality control", "patent", "functional food", and "product development". Records written in English or Chinese, as well as Chinese translations or annotated editions of classical Tibetan medical texts, were considered. Classical Tibetan medical texts, regional materia medica, Bai medicinal monographs, local chronicles, dissertations, and reference lists were additionally consulted to corroborate botanical features, traditional indications, and application-related information. Duplicate records, conference abstracts, editorials, studies unrelated to VTR, reports on other species without clear attribution to V. thibetica, records with low relevance, records for which the full text or complete information was unavailable, reports with insufficient or non-extractable information, records only incidentally mentioning VTR, and patents or formulas in which the role of VTR could not be clearly determined were excluded. Finally, 63 records, including journal articles, dissertations, monographs, local chronicles, and patent records, were included in this review. The literature selection process is shown in Figure 1. Chemical structures were drawn using ChemDraw, and schematic illustrations were prepared using Microsoft PowerPoint. Ethnopharmacological evidence indicates that VTR has long been used in Tibetan and Bai medicine as a tonic and medicinal food for fatigue relief, menstrual regulation, and cold-related disorders. Modern studies suggest potential anti-fatigue, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and gastrointestinal regulatory effects; however, current evidence remains largely based on crude extracts and experimental models, with limited validation of active compounds and molecular mechanisms. Phytochemical studies have identified several classes of constituents, including coumarins, phenylpropanoids, flavonoids, sterols, and polysaccharides, but their contribution to bioactivity remains insufficiently clarified. Quality standardization, safety evaluation, and product development remain major challenges for the rational utilization of VTR. V. thibetica is an alpine medicinal-food resource with important ethnopharmacological value and potential for further investigation. However, current research remains limited by insufficient phytochemical characterization, unclear structure-activity relationships, inadequate mechanistic investigations, and the lack of standardized quality evaluation systems. Further studies are needed to clarify its chemical basis, active constituents, pharmacological effects, quality standards, safety profile, and sustainable resource utilization, thereby promoting its scientific evaluation, standardization, and sustainable development.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Early Dose Reduction or Discontinuation Versus Antipsychotic Maintenance After First-Episode Psychosis: Results From the HAMLETT Study.
abstract: After remission from a first episode psychosis (FEP), international clinical guidelines recommend continuation of antipsychotic medication for at least 1 year, although many patients wish to reduce or discontinue medication due to side effects or long-term health concerns. Evidence on the cost-effectiveness of early dose reduction or discontinuation compared to continuation remains limited. A trial-based cost-utility analysis was conducted alongside the ongoing HAMLETT study, in which 347 remitted FEP participants were randomized to either early guided dose reduction or discontinuation or maintenance treatment for 1 year. Both healthcare and societal perspectives over a 24-month time horizon were considered. Health outcomes were expressed as quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) derived from the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire using Dutch valuation tariffs. Costs were estimated using patient reported healthcare utilization and administrative pharmacy data. Incremental costs and effects were analysed using seemingly unrelated regression with uncertainty assessed through nonparametric bootstrapping and multiple sensitivity analyses. Early dose reduction or discontinuation was associated with lower quality-adjusted life years and higher or comparable costs compared with maintenance treatment over the 2-year analysis period. In the base-case societal perspective analysis, incremental costs were €23,563 and incremental effects were -0.077 QALYs, resulting in an incremental net monetary benefit of -€27,430 at a willingness-to-pay threshold of €50,000 per QALY at 24 months. Results were consistent across several scenarios with only approximately 9% probability that early dose reduction or discontinuation was cost-effective at the assumed willingness-to-pay threshold. However, a sex-at-birth subgroup analysis suggested a small and uncertain positive incremental net monetary benefit among female participants. Over a 24-month period, early dose reduction or discontinuation of antipsychotic medication after remission from a FEP is unlikely to be cost-effective compared with maintenance treatment from both healthcare and societal perspectives. Whether longer term functional improvements associated with early dose reduction translate into cost-effective benefits remains uncertain and requires follow-up. EudraCT number: 2017-002406-12.

title: Open Dialogue: challenges in interpreting the ODDESSI trial results - Authors' reply.
Global, regional, and national burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases in 204 countries and territories, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
abstract: Gallbladder and biliary diseases-including cholelithiasis, cholecystitis, cholangitis, and other non-malignant biliary tract disorders-are important contributors to the global digestive disease burden, but a global, comprehensive, and systematic estimation of their burden is absent. We aimed to quantify long-term trends and current patterns in prevalence, mortality, and disability associated with gallbladder and biliary diseases across geographies, sexes, and ages. We used estimates from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 to assess the burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases in 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023. Mortality was modelled with the Cause of Death Ensemble model and prevalence with the Disease Modelling Meta-Regression tool (DisMod-MR 2.1). Years of life lost (YLLs) were calculated as the number of deaths for each age-sex-location-year multiplied by the standard life expectancy at each age. Severity-specific prevalence values were multiplied by their respective disability weights (with asymptomatic cases assigned zero disability) to estimate years lived with disability (YLDs). Disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) were computed by summing YLDs and YLLs. We report prevalence, mortality, YLDs, YLLs, and DALYs as counts and age-standardised and age-specific rates per 100 000 population with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs), stratified by sex, GBD region, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI). In 1990 and 2023, the global counts for prevalence attributable to gallbladder and biliary diseases were 157·4 million (95% UI 134·0 to 183·3) and 264·4 million (226·0 to 309·9), for deaths were 65 800 (95% UI 53 000 to 78 800) and 146 700 (121 800 to 171 300), and for DALYs were 4·8 million (95% UI 3·5 to 6·2) and 8·2 million (6·3 to 10·6), representing substantial increases. However, age-standardised rates declined over the same period, from 3573·2 (95% UI 3045·5 to 4159·1) per 100 000 population to 2990·1 (2561·5 to 3492·5) per 100 000 population for prevalence, from 1·95 (1·58 to 2·31) per 100 000 population to 1·67 (1·39 to 1·95) per 100 000 population for mortality, and from 111·5 (84·1 to 143·3) per 100 000 population to 92·3 (70·9 to 119·6) per 100 000 population for DALYs. Over the past three decades, females had higher age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates than males, while sex differences in mortality rates were smaller. In 2023, age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates were lowest in south Asia and highest in central and western Europe, central Asia, and many regions in Latin America. By contrast, several regions in sub-Saharan Africa had relatively low prevalence and DALY rates but comparatively high mortality rates. National patterns broadly mirrored these regional profiles. In 2023, prevalence and DALY counts peaked in middle to early-older adulthood (ages 55-69 years), but age-specific rates continued to rise into the oldest age groups, with DALYs dominated by YLDs in midlife and early-older adulthood and by YLLs at older ages (≥80 years). The number of deaths peaked in the ninth decade of life, but age-specific rates also peaked in the oldest age groups. Across GBD regions, the association between SDI and age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates generally followed a reversed U-shaped pattern, with the lowest rates at low SDI, peak rates at intermediate SDI, and declining rates at the highest SDI levels. The association between SDI and mortality rate was less clear. The global burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases is rising in absolute terms despite declining age-standardised rates, underscoring the importance of population growth and ageing. Health systems, particularly in settings with rapidly ageing populations and intermediate SDI levels, will need to expand diagnostic, elective, and emergency surgical capacity while investing in prevention of obesity and metabolic risk factors. Marked regional and national heterogeneity, as well as differences in risk factors, might reflect variance in health-system capacity and access to care, including timely diagnosis, availability of surgical services, and perioperative care. The predominance of non-fatal disability in midlife and rising mortality in older age groups indicates that integrated strategies spanning risk-factor control, early diagnosis, elective management, and robust acute care for older adults are essential to reduce both YLDs and YLLs. Gates Foundation.

title: Breathlessness mechanisms, measurement, and management in adults: evidence update on behalf of The Dyspnoea Society.
abstract: Breathlessness affects an estimated 40% of adults living with chronic disease, with substantial consequences for individuals, carers, and health-care systems. This Dyspnoea Society Research Statement, developed for researchers, clinicians, and adults living with or caring for someone with breathlessness, provides a state-of-the-art synthesis of recent advances in chronic breathlessness mechanisms, measurement, and management, and outlines a research agenda for the next decade. Key advancements include establishment of neural respiratory drive as a mechanistic contributor to exertional breathlessness; neuroimaging evidence that breathlessness arises from integration of peripheral and central processes within a dynamic brain network involving sensorimotor and cognitive-affective regions, supporting behavioural and psychosocial interventions; and improved measurement through responsive multidimensional instruments and approaches to quantify symptom abnormality relative to physical activity. Evidence supports early use of low-risk, non-pharmacological interventions for management of breathlessness, whereas evidence for pharmacological therapies is limited in most situations. Health-care redesign, including symptom-focused diagnostic pathways, integrated care models, and disease-agnostic breathlessness services, might help to improve patient outcomes while reducing health-care costs.

title: P2RX7 drives inflammatory microglia and pathogenic extracellular vesicle secretion in tauopathy.
abstract: P2X purinoreceptor 7 (P2RX7), an ATP-gated ion channel, contributes to Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression, but its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we show that genetic disruption of P2rx7 mitigates brain atrophy, tau accumulation, and cognitive impairment in PS19 mice. Microglia-specific, but not astrocyte-specific, deletion of P2rx7 suppresses tau propagation. Single-cell RNA sequencing identifies a previously unrecognized first-responding microglial state (FRM) with prominent P2rx7 expression. P2RX7 promotes the transition from FRM to an inflammatory microglial state enriched in extracellular vesicle (EV) biogenesis. P2RX7 increases EV loading of tau and of mitochondrial proteins and DNA, which activate cytosolic DNA sensing and interferon signaling in recipient microglia. Tau-containing microglial EVs disrupt neuronal endolysosomal integrity and facilitate endosomal tau escape and phosphorylation. Thus, P2RX7 regulates the FRM branch point, driving inflammatory microglial transition and EV-mediated spread of tau and toxic mitochondrial molecules and highlighting the P2RX7-EV axis as a therapeutic target in AD.

title: Tumor-to-dendritic cell reprogramming induces immunogenic lymphoid structures across cancers.
abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) in tumors are associated with improved responses to immunotherapy. Here, we examined the impact of type 1 conventional dendritic cells (cDC1s) in TLS formation. Reprogrammed tumor cells into cDC1-like cells remodeled the tumor microenvironment and induced immunogenic TLSs (imgTLSs) across melanoma, colon, bladder, breast, and pancreatic cancer models with distinct genetic backgrounds. cDC1-like cells activated lymphotoxin, TNF, and interferon programs and engaged early with T cells through MHC class I and CD40 signaling to induce imgTLSs containing BCL6+ germinal centers, independently of endogenous cDC1s. Intratumoral positioning shaped distinct cDC1-like cell states, with DC-LAMP+ CCR7+ migratory cDC1s nucleating niches enriched in CD4+, CD8+ T cells, and B cells in mouse and human tumors. ImgTLSs sustained B and T cell responses and promoted systemic immunity through expansion of shared clonotypes in distant, untreated tumors. Our findings outline the spatial organization, signaling programs and interactions of cDC1-like cells that initiate intratumoral lymphoid structures and establish cellular reprogramming as a strategy toward overcoming resistance to immunotherapy.

title: Retraction to "Integrative ALS therapy: gene targeted therapy by base editing and potential exercise rehabilitation as synergistic strategies for functional recovery".
Anti-CD20 mediated B cell depletion exerts a distinct influence on T cell immunity by decreasing effector memory CD4 Th17 and Th1.17 subsets in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is driven by dysregulated B and T cell interactions. Anti-CD20 B cell depletion with rituximab (RTX) strongly suppresses MS disease activity, yet how it relates to T cell immunity is unclear. We analysed clinically acquired flow cytometry data from 310 people with MS before and six months after RTX initiation, with plasma proteomics and CD4 T cell receptor sequencing in subgroups. Baseline T cell profiles correlated with B cell numbers, age, and HLA-DRB1*15:01 status. To limit confounding from prior therapies, RTX-associated changes were primarily assessed in treatment-naïve participants, in whom effector memory Th17 and Th1.17 CD4 subsets were selectively reduced, while CD8 subsets, the plasma inflammatory proteome, and CD4 clonality were largely unchanged. This observational study cannot establish causality, but identifies distinct memory CD4 subsets, relevant to MS disease activity, that are measurable in routine clinical flow cytometry.

title: HIF-3α beyond the dominant-negative paradigm: Isoform diversity, species divergence, and redox-driven diseases.
abstract: Hypoxia-inducible factor 3 alpha (HIF-3α) has long been considered a minor, inhibitory branch of the HIF pathway. However, accumulating evidence suggests that HIF-3α is a context-dependent regulator with transcriptional activator and dominant-negative functions. The human HIF3A locus undergoes extensive alternative splicing, yielding at least eight to ten protein isoforms. In contrast, the mouse Hif3a gene produces only three major variants. This creates substantial species divergence in isoform architecture and expression. Full-length human isoforms, such as HIF-3α1, HIF-3α2, and HIF-3α9, are bona fide transcription factors that regulate both canonical and non-canonical hypoxic targets, including EPO, LC3C, REDD1, SQRDL, and IGFBP-1. In contrast, truncated variants, such as HIF-3α4, antagonize HIF-1/2-dependent angiogenic and metabolic programs in a tissue-specific manner. Mouse models demonstrate that canonical HIF-3α integrates developmental and redox cues in the lungs, heart, and metabolism. Furthermore, human HIF3A methylation and isoform-specific expression have been linked to obesity, liver dysfunction, diabetes, chronic lung disease, neurodegeneration, and cancer. Full-length isoforms often promote tumor growth and metastasis (e.g., in colorectal and pancreatic cancers), whereas truncated isoforms constrain angiogenesis or stabilize oncogenic HIF-2α in certain contexts. In this review, we integrate these findings into an isoform-resolved, cross-species framework that distinguishes experimentally validated HIF-3α functions from indirect associations and proposed redox mechanisms. We propose that HIF-3α acts less as a single hypoxia transcription factor and more as an isoform-specific rheostat that shapes acute, chronic, and redox-stressed states. Finally, we outline the need for long-read transcriptomics, isoform-specific assays, evidence-stratified disease models, and targeted modulation of individual HIF-3α variants to translate this complexity into therapeutic strategies for redox-driven human diseases.

title: Protein adduction by multiple aldehydes contributes to α-synuclein aggregation and dopaminergic neuron loss in rat models of Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Dopaminergic neurodegeneration in the substantia nigra causes the motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD). The mechanisms underlying this neurodegeneration remain unclear. Aldehydes exhibit high reactivity that can covalently modify functional proteins and cause cell damage. This study aimed to characterize protein adduction by endogenous aldehydes and investigate its role in dopaminergic neuron loss in PD. Forty free aldehydes were identified in rat models of PD induced by 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA) and rotenone using chemical isotope labeling coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry. Twenty-two aldehydes were found in the rat brain for the first time. In addition to lipid peroxidation, amine oxidation was the major source of aldehydes. Levels of 27 aldehyde-protein adducts in the substantia nigra and striatum were increased by 1- to 5-fold at 4-6 h after 6-OHDA injection. Consistently, most of these protein adducts were significantly increased in the rotenone model. Application of the trapping reagent phenelzine and the aldehyde dehydrogenase-2 activator Alda-1 reduced protein adduction by aldehydes and attenuated neuron loss induced by 6-OHDA injection. Twelve aldehydes covalently modified α-synuclein in 6-OHDA-treated rats, with the lysine residue in the GLSK peptide identified as the primary binding target. Aldehydes caused peptide crosslinking and aggregation of α-synuclein. Additive effects of covalent modification by aldehydes contributed to neuron death. Collectively, protein adduction by multiple aldehydes contributes to α-synuclein aggregation and dopaminergic neuron loss in rat models of PD. Multiple biogenic aldehydes, especially those from abnormal oxidation of amines, represent a novel class of toxic molecules that play a pathogenic role in PD.

title: MRI before CSF: prospective evidence that the 2024 McDonald criteria reduce lumbar punctures.
abstract: The 2024 McDonald criteria for the diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (MS) introduced MRI biomarkers including the central vein sign (CVS), which may substitute for cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) testing in certain circumstances. We evaluated how the sequential application of MRI biomarkers incorporated into the 2024 criteria changes the need for CSF examination. Our primary analysis used the DECISIve cohort, a prospective, multicentre study of patients with typical clinically isolated syndrome who all required lumbar puncture (LP) for diagnosis under 2017 MS diagnostic criteria. Participants received both LP and MRI with T2* susceptibility-based imaging. We applied the 2024 criteria sequentially, evaluating MRI topographies and CVS status prior to determining whether LP was still required. To assess generalisability, we evaluated a separate consecutive single-centre real-world cohort. In DECISIve (n=98), 70% (69/98) could be diagnosed without LP under 2024 criteria when MRI with CVS analysis was performed first: 21% (21/98) had lesions in ≥4 topographies, 72% (48/67) with 2-3 topographies were CVS-positive. In the real-world cohort (n=87), 69% (60/87) met the 2024 criteria without LP, consistent with the trial finding. There was significant concordance between paraclinical tests in DECISIve: 90% (19/21) of participants with ≥4 topographies were also CVS-positive, and 81% (56/69) of OCB-positive participants were CVS-positive. Only 11% (10/88) of participants with at least two topographies were solely OCB-positive. Assessing MRI with CVS first removes the need for LP in most patients, a finding corroborated in real-world practice. Collaborative effort is needed to develop CVS/PRL expertise across centres.

title: Dinotefuran aggravates Alzheimer's disease-associated microglial inflammation through the CHUK/NFKB1-mediated NF-κB signaling pathway.
journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
abstract: Neonicotinoid pesticides are widely used systemic insecticides with increasing evidence of neurotoxicity. However, their potential contribution to Alzheimer's disease (AD)-related neuroinflammation remains poorly understood. In this study, seven representative neonicotinoid pesticides were systematically evaluated by integrating physicochemical characterization, target prediction, pathway enrichment analysis, human AD snRNA-seq, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and experimental validation. Among the seven compounds, dinotefuran was prioritized based on its favorable blood-brain barrier permeability and enrichment in inflammation-related pathways. Integration of target prediction with AD transcriptomic analyses identified CHUK and NFKB1 as key candidate targets associated with NF-κB signaling. snRNA-seq analysis further demonstrated preferential enrichment of NF-κB signaling activity in microglia from AD brains. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations supported potential interactions between dinotefuran and IKKα (CHUK) as well as NF-κB1 (p50). In Aβ-treated BV2 microglia, dinotefuran further enhanced activation of the CHUK/NFKB1-mediated NF-κB signaling pathway, accompanied by increased expression of IKKα, phosphorylation of IκBα and p65, enhanced NF-κB1 activation, and elevated secretion of IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, IFN-α, and IFN-β. These pro-inflammatory effects were markedly attenuated by the NF-κB inhibitor BAY11-7082. Collectively, our findings suggest that CHUK/NFKB1-associated NF-κB signaling may contribute to dinotefuran-enhanced inflammatory responses in Aβ-treated BV2 microglia, providing preliminary mechanistic insights into the potential involvement of neonicotinoid pesticides in AD-related neuroinflammation.
